subject: SLA exception: private edge responsibility matrix — Sedgewell Therapeutics
messages:
From: Evan Morales <evan.morales@sedgewell.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment SLA ask — Sedgewell clinical edge

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the walkthrough the other day. We're moving forward with an on-prem connector for our lab sites (pilot: three hospitals) and need to align contract language around SLA attribution and exceptions where Sedgewell controls the network and on-prem compute.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood provide an "accountability matrix" that maps uptime/latency obligations to the responsible party for each component (Redwood runtime, on-prem gateway, customer LAN, third-party peering)?
- We need proposed contract language that limits Redwood SLA credits where the customer-managed infra is the proximate cause (e.g., WAN flaps, local firewall rules, KMS egress delays).
- Any operational playbook for detection and evidence we should collect from our ops team to trigger escalations?

We expect to share a short SOC / network diagram and would like this formalized as an attachment to the MSA as an appendix. Time-sensitive — procurement is pushing for language this week.

Appreciate your help,

Evan Morales
Director, IT Procurement
Sedgewell Therapeutics
attachments: none inline (will send topology diagram separately)

Karthik: could you draft the initial accountability matrix and recommended carve language (short paragraph + sample appendix)?
Soojin: we'll need legal sign-off on the wording — please flag anything that looks risky from a compliance perspective.
Lauren: loop in solutions engineering for the playbook steps and evidence we should ask the customer to provide.

I'll consolidate and send back to Evan.

Thanks — Priya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment SLA ask — Sedgewell clinical edge

PRIYA / team — draft attached. Key points:

1) Accountability matrix (attached spreadsheet "sedgewell-sla-matrix-v1.xlsx"): maps components (API gateway, Redwood runtime, local on-prem gateway, customer LAN, third-party ISP, KMS) to owner and example evidence. We recommend a two-tier attribution: direct (Redwood) vs. customer-controlled. For mixed faults, we propose proportional credit allocation where telemetry shows clear tokenization of responsibilities.

2) Sample contract appendix language (short excerpt below):
"Where Customer operates or materially controls the network, compute, or key management components used to access Redwood services (collectively, "Customer-Controlled Infrastructure"), Redwood's latency and availability SLAs shall exclude downtime or degraded performance caused by Customer-Controlled Infrastructure. Customer agrees to provide diagnostic evidence (network logs, traceroutes, timestamped gateway logs, and KMS audit events) upon request to enable attribution. In instances where multiple parties contribute to the incident, the parties will engage in a joint post-incident attribution review and agree on proportional service credit."

3) Evidence playbook (one-page included in the PDF): what Sedgewell ops should collect (timestamped traceroutes, gateway syslogs, BGP / peering event dumps, KMS request timings, sample request IDs so Redwood can correlate). We also included an escalation contact matrix and a two-step verification checklist for Red/Amber/Green triage.

I left open a narrow carve: Redwood will still accept connectivity tests (prefix pings, small request traces) and may apply a short-running remote diagnostic to validate whether the issue is within Redwood's network. If those diagnostics are blocked by firewall policy, attribution will defer to the evidence provided by Customer.

Attaching: sedgewell-sla-matrix-v1.xlsx, sedgewell-deployment-notes.pdf

Let me know if you want stronger guardrails around KMS-timeouts — we can add an explicit egress ceiling and an evidence threshold.

-Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 10:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment SLA ask — Sedgewell clinical edge

Thanks Karthik — quick review from Legal / Security:
- Language looks consistent with our prior private-deployment appendices but: please replace "proportional service credit" with a clearer mechanism (example: a two-step adjudication where Redwood issues provisional credit limited to incidents where Redwood telemetry proves >70% responsibility; otherwise, credits are withheld until joint adjudication).
- Add explicit commitment: Redwood will retain request-level trace IDs for 30 days for incident correlation (customer may request extended retention under a separate SOW).
- For KMS/egress: recommend adding a diagnostic SLA of 120s for KMS roundtrip where applicable; if the customer's KMS consistently responds slower than 120s causing degradation, the incident will be presumed customer-responsible absent contrary evidence.
- Minor edit: change "Customer agrees to provide diagnostic evidence" to "Customer shall provide reasonable diagnostic evidence" to avoid unlimited burden.

I can sign off once we add those clarifications.

Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

- Legal added a provisional-adjudication mechanism and an explicit 30-day trace retention for correlation.
- KMS diagnostic threshold: 120s (see section 2.3).

Attachments: sedgewell-sla-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix), sedgewell-deployment-notes.pdf (evidence playbook), redwood-private-appendix-draft.docx (contract appendix draft).

Next steps: please review and let us know any redlines by EOD Monday; if that works, we'll have legal prepare the appendix for MSA attachment and circulate via DocuSign. If you prefer, we can run a joint 30-minute session to walk the Sedgewell ops team through the evidence playbook.

Thanks — Priya
